title: Ines and the Crown
premise: Ines Ishikawa keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in stolen memories, bottled dreams, and other impossible things. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Ines discovers the child carries a fragment of the Covenant — the ancient pact binding the human realm to the moonlit Otherworld — and that the guild's masters have been quietly devouring covenant-memories to fuel their power. Hunted by her own employers and shadowed by a moon that wanes toward its thirteenth turn, Ines must gather the scattered fragments, confront the guildmaster who stole her own childhood memories, and reforge the Covenant at the Moonwell before the last turn seals both realms in silence. She succeeds at terrible cost: her ledger-memory is spent as the final fragment, and she ends the book unable to remember why the child calls her mother.
about_author: Paloma Iversen is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters no one claimed, an experience she credits for her obsession with what records fail to hold. She writes from a coastal town where the fog arrives on schedule, and insists it keeps better appointments than most people.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Ines audits the Vellum Guild's vaults, cataloguing bottled griefs and borrowed years, establishing her precision and quiet detachment. Her POV. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness — she trusts ink more than people, and we learn she has gaps in her own past she refuses to examine.

chapters.title: A Knock Before Dawn
chapters.summary: A mud-streaked child appears at the guild door during a curfew, speaking a language no scribe recognizes — yet Ines finds herself half-understanding it, which terrifies her. Her POV. The beat is reluctant recognition: something in the child's voice scratches at a memory Ines doesn't have.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buys Cheap
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane orders the child held 'for appraisal.' Ines, translating under duress, realizes the child speaks of a broken Covenant and a moon counting turns. Her POV. The beat is dawning complicity — she has been bookkeeping for predators without reading the entries closely.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: An old astronomer-poet, Sef, deciphers the child's words: when the moon completes its thirteenth turn, the realms sever, and everything the Covenant sustained — magic, memory, mercy — unravels. Alternating Ines and Sef POVs. The beat is dread converting into resolve.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Stolen Childhood
chapters.summary: Ines discovers a vial in the deep archive labeled with her own name — her missing years, sold by someone with guild access. Her POV. The beat is vertigo; the thief learns she was robbed first, and her careful neutrality cracks into fury.

chapters.title: The Night Market
chapters.summary: Ines smuggles the child out through the Night Market, trading favors with fence-witches and a ferryman who accepts memories as fare. Child's POV (rendered through Ines's translation). The beat is fragile trust forming between two people who cannot fully speak.

chapters.title: Hounds of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Corvane sends retrievers — clerks weaponized with consumed memories — to reclaim the child. A rooftop chase ends with Ines burning a page of the master ledger to cover their escape. Her POV. The beat is the point of no return; she is now a thief of her own guild.

chapters.title: Sef's Observatory
chapters.summary: At Sef's cliffside observatory, the child draws the Covenant's map in starlight: five fragments scattered across the realm, each guarded by a keeper who traded their memory of guarding it. Sef's POV. The beat is awe shadowed by guilt — Sef once refused to help the last covenant-bearer.

chapters.title: The Keeper Who Forgot Herself
chapters.summary: First fragment: a bridge-keeper who sold her name and now guards a door she can't explain. Ines must give her a memory back — one of Ines's own precious few. Her POV. The beat is sacrifice as practice; the theme of inheritance becomes literal.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Corvane corners Ines alone: he'll return her stolen childhood intact if she delivers the child. He reveals the guild devours covenant-memories to hoard power beyond the severance. Her POV. The beat is temptation sharpened by truth — her old life offered back at the price of a new one.

chapters.title: What the Child Remembers
chapters.summary: Through shared dream-contact, Ines sees the child's origin: born of the Otherworld, sent across as a living fragment when the Covenant first cracked. Child's POV via Ines. The beat is heartbreak — the child chose exile to save both worlds, and asks Ines nothing in return.

chapters.title: The Drowned Archive
chapters.summary: Second fragment lies in a flooded library guarded by a librarian made of every book ever unwritten. Ines bargains using her ledger-craft, but loses Sef's oldest poem as payment. Her POV. The beat is cost accumulating; victory that feels like erosion.

chapters.title: Turn Nine
chapters.summary: The moon's ninth turn brings tide-magic surging into the city; ordinary people begin forgetting loved ones mid-sentence. Sef's POV from the observatory, charting the acceleration. The beat is escalating stakes made intimate — the apocalypse measured in small amnesias.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Bone Orchard
chapters.summary: The ferryman, bought back by Corvane, sells their route. Retrievers ambush them; Sef is captured buying time. Ines escapes with the child and two fragments. Her POV. The beat is grief and rage braided together — and the realization Corvane wants her specifically, not just the child.

chapters.title: The Master's Memory Palace
chapters.summary: Infiltrating Corvane's estate, Ines finds his vault: thousands of consumed lives arranged like a garden, including her parents' memories. She learns Corvane was the apprentice who sold her childhood to fund his ascent. Her POV. The beat is cold clarity — vengeance and duty pointing the same direction.

chapters.title: Rescue at the Turning Stair
chapters.summary: Ines frees Sef, who has resisted consumption by reciting the poem he lost — kept alive in him by stubbornness. Third fragment recovered from Corvane's own keeping. Sef's POV. The beat is defiant hope; memory as resistance rather than possession.

chapters.title: Twelfth Turn: The Waning City
chapters.summary: With one turn left, the city dims; colors drain, names fade from signs. The child weakens as the fragment inside them strains toward the severance. Ines's POV. The beat is urgency fused with tenderness — she has come to love the child she may have to spend.

chapters.title: The Price of the Fourth Fragment
chapters.summary: The fourth fragment rests in the Moonwell's antechamber, guarded by a mirror that demands a whole life's memory as toll. Ines pays with her guild years — every entry she ever kept. Her POV. The beat is liberation disguised as loss; she emerges lighter and unmoored.

chapters.title: Corvane at the Well
chapters.summary: Corvane arrives with his retrievers to consume the final fragment himself and rule whatever survives the severance. Confrontation at the wellhead; Sef holds the hounds with the restored poem while Ines faces her past's architect. Shared POV. The beat is the climax's opening blow.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Climax: Ines offers her deepest remaining memory — the true one, of bearing the child — as the fifth fragment, completing the Covenant as the thirteenth turn closes. Corvane, lunging to seize it, is unmade by the well's judgment. The realms knit; light returns. Ines's POV. The beat is transcendence through surrender.

chapters.title: After the Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Dawn over a mended world. The child, whole again, speaks both languages — and calls Ines by a name Ines no longer recognizes as hers. Sef begins a new chronicle. Ines's POV. The beat is bittersweet peace: she saved everything except her reason for saving it.

chapters.title: A New Ledger
chapters.summary: Resolution: Ines opens a blank book and writes only the child's name on the first page, choosing to build memory forward instead of mourning backward. The child takes her hand. Her POV. The beat is earned hope — inheritance redefined as what we give, not what we keep.
